text:
Maria G.: FYI canary rollout 2026-03-18 09:14UTC failing in eu-central. ALB target group shows 5/12 unhealthy and pods are getting connection resets from health checks. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/cloud/targets/abc123

infra-bot: Deploy canary/2026-03-18-09:13 -> FAILED (target_health: 5/12)

Ben K.: do we have the SG rules for the node ENIs? can you paste `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids <sg>` output for the node sg and alb sg?

Maria G.: quick paste of the node SG ingress we deployed in the template:```"SecurityGroupIngress": [{"IpProtocol":"tcp","FromPort":8443,"ToPort":8443,"CidrIp":"10.2.0.0/16"}]```I was trying to limit to internal subnet, assuming ALB would be in same VPC. Apparently the ALB is in a peered VPC for eu-central (weird infra routing choice).

Jae L.: ahhh, that explains it. ALB is using SG `sg-0a11bc22` in the peered account and the node SG was only allowing the local CIDR, so traffic from the ALB's ENIs is dropped. We accidentally locked the health checks to the wrong source. The ALB health checks come from the ALB SG, not from a predictable IP range.

Priya S.: short workaround: add an ingress rule to the node SG referencing the ALB SG as the source. example:```aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-node-0123 --protocol tcp --port 8443 --source-group sg-0a11bc22```That will allow the ALB ENIs to reach pods. We should make the CloudFormation change after rollback.

Ben K.: if you want a quick test without infra change, you can curl the node IP from a bastion in the peered VPC or run a tcpdump on one node:```kubectl exec -ti debug-ssh -- tcpdump -n -i any port 8443```But adding the SG reference is minimal blast radius.

Maria G.: applied the inbound rule referencing `sg-0a11bc22` for the node group and restarted the target group registration. Running a probe now...

infra-bot: TargetGroup tg-eu-central: health check state -> 12/12 healthy (09:16:50 UTC)

Maria G.: ✅ all healthy now. leaving canary running for 10m and will promote if stable. Will open a tiny infra PR to change the CF template to use the ALB SG reference instead of fixed cidr. Thanks for the quick help :raised_hands: 

Jae L.: filed follow-up: add test coverage for cross-account ALBs and doc note about "always reference ALB SG for healthcheck ports". low risk but good to have.

Priya S.: Also adding a short runbook step: when TG shows < 100% healthy, check SG source-group vs expected ALB SG before touching NACLs.

Ben K.: nice recovery. also let's audit other stacks for the same pattern — I remember a few stacks copy-pasted the ingress cidr. :mag:
